description: CAL-2 is named the neutron beta-decay WIDTH D_beta, and the corpus asserts Q_beta = hbar/D_beta with Q_beta a 0.784 MeV Q-value. Both cannot hold: if D_beta is the width then hbar/D_beta is the LIFETIME (878.4 s), and if D_beta := hbar/Q_beta then it is 24 orders of magnitude from that lifetime. The framework computes the decay's ENERGY RELEASE, not its RATE. This RETRACTS the interpretive claim of PR #6687/#6700 that candidate (iii)'s obstacle was already satisfied; (iii) returns to open.
q0AnchorReason: AGENTS.md 2026-08-07 owner directive: proton is the default for all new compute

data.corpus_assertion: Q_beta = hbar/D_beta, D_beta = 'the neutron beta-decay width'
data.tau_n_source: PDG 2022, bottle average; the beam-bottle discrepancy is ~8 s and is irrelevant at 24 orders of magnitude
data.reading_R1: D_beta := Gamma_n  =>  hbar/D_beta = tau_n = 878.4 s, a TIME, so it cannot be the 0.784 MeV Q-value the corpus says it is
data.what_stands: Q_beta as a CAL-2 proxy, reproduced to 0.17 %. A Q-value is fixed by mass differences alone.
data.what_is_missing: the RATE. A width additionally needs the coupling and the phase-space integral -- precisely what candidate (iii) asked for and what the framework has not supplied.
data.retraction: PR #6687 and the block edit in #6700 claim (iii)'s obstacle was satisfied because D_beta IS CAL-2. The Lean and arithmetic of #6687 stand -- they concern two width MECHANISMS and are pure mathematics. The interpretive step does not. Candidate (iii) returns to OPEN with its obstacle sharpened: the missing object is not a decay observable but specifically the rate.
data.scope: (a) throughout. Nothing here says Im(q) DOES encode a width; it says the reciprocal mechanism does not produce the one width we can check, so the argument by which I narrowed (iii) does not hold.
data.not_a_rename_proposal: the naming is the author's, was flagged to the author, and the author's ruling is pending. This probe measures the gap rather than resolving it.
